title: Seasonality in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
one_line: Stocks that did well in a given calendar month tend to do well in the same month in later years, for up to 20 years (decile spreads > 60 bps/month, NYSE/AMEX 1963-2002).

findings.statement: Same-calendar-month returns persist up to 20 years; decile spreads > 60 bps/month.
Positive in all 12 months; strongest in January, above average in October and December.
findings.evidence: Not explained by size, industry or earnings timing.

reported_results.headline: Stocks that did well in a given calendar month tend to do well in the same month in later years, for up to 20 years (decile spreads > 60 bps/month, NYSE/AMEX 1963-2002).

data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
